factors.title: Falling electronics prices
factors.text: **Walmart reports:** “Within entertainment, deflation continues to impact sales growth in electronics.” (Walmart FY13 Q2 earnings call transcript, 2012-08-16). Across all 45 stores, Electronics was −0.5% this quarter, so company-wide trends explain only part of this store's −12.7%.

factors.title: A problem at this store
factors.text: **Sales data:** Store 7 Electronics fell −12.7% this quarter (down 9 of 13 weeks), while other Colorado stores held up much better: Store 16 −3.6%, Store 41 +2.8%, Store 32 +14.2%. Likely the store itself: stock, product range or local competition.

factors.title: Fewer promotions during back-to-school
factors.text: **Sales data:** Store 7 ran fewer markdowns than usual that week (about 0.6× a normal week), while the **Federal Reserve** reported “Home furnishings, clothing and back-to-school items sold well, while sales of high-end jewelry were weaker.” (Kansas City Fed (10th District)).

factors.title: Ruled out
factors.text: No holiday that week, fuel prices barely changed (+2.1%), normal weather, and the rest of the store was only −3.3%.

EXC-S07-D72-20120824.bottom_line: Walmart reported only a small company-wide decline in this category, but Store 7 Electronics fell −12.7% this quarter. Falling prices explain a small part; most of the drop is specific to Store 7.
review: Confirm whether Electronics unit volume held (price effect) or fell (demand loss).
Evaluate whether markdown spend in this period produced any lift for Electronics.
Compare with other Colorado stores: Store 16 −11.1%, Store 41 −0.5%.
limitations: Department and region names are publicly inferred, not confirmed by Walmart.
The store fell much more than the chain, and public reports only describe company-wide trends, so part of the drop is unexplained.
No unit or price data, so price deflation and lost volume cannot be separated.

Reports describe Walmart or the Fed district as a whole, not this store.

EXC-S13-D01-20120420.explanation: The Candy & Tobacco sales drop at your store was not a real problem but an explained pattern caused by Easter timing. Easter fell on April 8 in 2012 versus April 24 in 2011, so the holiday-driven sales peak shifted into an earlier week, leaving this week's comparison against last year's pre-Easter rush. As Walmart noted on its FY13 Q1 earnings call, "This year, Easter benefitted the first quarter, but will pressure sales in the second quarter." All 45 stores in the region saw similar declines, and Candy & Tobacco is actually up 1.2% this quarter, confirming the dip reflects calendar timing rather than a store-level issue.

factors.title: Christmas inflated the baseline
factors.text: **Sales data:** the expected $2.46M is the average of Dec 9–30, which includes Christmas week ($3.22M, 1.8× a typical week of $1.84M). Against the same week last year, Store 2 is +2.4% ($1.80M vs. $1.76M), and the same method would have flagged last year's week too (−30.9%).

factors.title: Every store dropped
factors.text: **Sales data:** all 45 stores fell a median −25.3% against their own 4-week baseline; Store 2 ranks 20th of 45. The five biggest shortfalls (Toys, Electronics, Media & Gaming, Impulse, Seasonal) all peak in Nov–Dec and are together +2.0% vs. last year's same week.

factors.title: Strong season, not a slump
factors.text: **Walmart reports:** “We completed a very successful holiday season, with strong sales during Thanksgiving week and throughout December.” (Walmart FY12 Q4 earnings call transcript, 2012-02-21). **Federal Reserve** (Dallas Fed (11th District)): “Jewelry, small electronics and apparel were areas of strength in retail this holiday season.”

factors.title: Still worth a look
factors.text: **Sales data:** Toys is −13.8% vs. last year's same week. Walmart said layaway lifted toy sales earlier in the quarter, so some demand may have been pulled forward. Possible, not confirmed.

factors.title: Ruled out
factors.text: A store-specific slump: the next 4 weeks are −0.9% vs. last year. Fuel (+6.1%) and weather (47°F vs. 45°F) were normal. Markdowns ($53.0K, 1.9× an average week) are recorded for the store, not by department, so they cannot explain the gap.

EXC-S02-ALL-20120106.bottom_line: Likely not a real problem. The expected number is inflated by Christmas week; compared with last year Store 2 is +2.4% and every store dropped. The detector's "structural slump" flag is not supported. Only Toys is worth a look over the next two weeks.
review: No store action needed for this week; use a same-week-last-year or holiday-aware baseline for January weeks.
Check Toys over the next two weeks (−13.8% vs. last year).
limitations: The detector's "structural slump" and "internal merchandising failure" reading comes from a baseline that is not adjusted for the Christmas peak; last year's comparison does not support it.
